quote: Ferner welche Functionen $p$ ten Grades $x^{p}+p\varphi(x)$ können mit Hülfe von $p^2-p$ [?] und $p^{r}$ zerlegt werden; welche mit Hülfe von $p^2-p p-p$ [?].
english: Further, which functions of degree $p$, $x^{p}+p\varphi(x)$, can be decomposed with the help of $p^2-p$ and $p^{r}$; which with the help of $p^2-p p-p$.
topic: The page ends a remark about Poincaré polygons whose opposite circular arcs are carried into each other, then poses questions on the irreducibility of x^{p^2}-px-p modulo (p^2, p) and on decomposing functions of degree p into linear factors modulo powers of p.

triage.modern_statement: The transcription is partly garbled: 'p^2-p' and 'p^2-p p-p' are marked [?]. A plausible reading is this. Take polynomials f(x)=x^p+p·φ(x) of degree p that reduce to x^p mod p, with φ in Z[x]. Which of them split into linear factors (or factor at all) modulo higher powers p^r, i.e. over Z/p^r Z or Z_p? Which of them stay irreducible, as the companion question about x^{p^2}-px-p suggests? In modern terms this is about factoring polynomials over the p-adic integers, the ramification of p in Q[x]/(f), and Newton polygons. It is not a single well-defined problem but an exploratory question from Hilbert's work on algebraic number fields (Zahlbericht era).
triage.answered_by: There is no direct answer to this specific note. The general question (how a polynomial factors over Z_p or modulo p^r, and how p decomposes in the field it defines) was handled by the Newton polygon method of Ø. Ore (1920s, 1928). Ore conjectured that an algorithm existed. Montes and later Guàrdia–Montes–Nart (2008–2012) provided one with higher-order Newton polygons, and with Pauli added single-factor lifting for factorization modulo prescribed powers of p. For Eisenstein-type cases where φ(0) is not divisible by p, Eisenstein's criterion already gives irreducibility.

evidence.claim: In a pioneering work in the 1920s, Ore conjectured that there is an algorithm to compute the prime ideal decomposition of p in Q[x]/(g), using Newton polygon analysis.
Guàrdia, Montes and Nart developed higher-order arithmetic Newton polygons, which give the factorization of a separable polynomial over a p-adic field.
The Montes algorithm combined with single-factor lifting factors F modulo m^ν to any prescribed precision ν over local fields.
Single-factor lifting combined with the Montes algorithm gives a fast factorization algorithm for polynomials over local fields.

triage.why: The note is fragmentary and the key moduli are uncertain transcriptions, so the exact question cannot be pinned down. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem, and I found no source discussing this note. What it asks about in substance, factoring x^p+pφ(x) modulo powers of p and p-adically, is settled in general by Ore's Newton polygon theory and the Montes/OM algorithms. Research on computing p-adic factorizations and prime ideal decompositions with Newton polygons is still active.
